Welcome toBodiam CE Primary School
A very warm welcome to Bodiam Church of England Primary School. Bodiam is a Church of England Voluntary Controlled School, where traditional values combine with an exciting modern curriculum to enable each of our children to fulfil their unique potential. We have a well-established caring ethos which contributes to the wonderful family feel to our school; the smiling faces and laughter you hear when you visit us, along with the excellent work throughout the school is a testament to this.
We are federated with Etchingham C E Primary School as part of the Riverside Federation. This collaborative working arrangement is a key driver in our pursuit of excellence so that we meet the needs and aspirations of all our pupils.
Our vision for our Christian community at the Riverside Federation is that our pupils feel valued for who they are, reach their full potential through high quality, inspirational learning experiences and are ready for life in an ever-changing world. We aim to treat everyone in our community with compassion, friendship and tolerance, and instil high aspirations for all, underpinned by the teaching that we 'love our neighbour as ourselves' (Mark 12:31).
We hope you find the information on this website useful. Please do not hesitate to contact us to discuss any other information you may need.
Cherane MarshallExecutive Headteacher

French
Intent
Our pupils will be confident reflective learners who recognise the rich opportunities learning languages brings to experiencing other countries and cultures.
A different language is a different version of life.
Implementation
Our French curriculum encapsulates the National Curriculum and is designed to show and enable the progression of skills and knowledge across Key Stage 2. We organise this teaching and learning across a two-year cycle to cater for our mixed-age classes.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodiam Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Intent
Our pupils will think like musicians. They will develop singing, performing, composing and listening skills and will explore a broad repertoire of musical genres from past and present. They will develop a love of music and explore their talent as musicians. They will leave us as creative, confident children.
Music gives a soul to the universe, wings to the mind, flight to the imagination and life to everything.
Implementation
Our Music curriculum encapsulates the National Curriculum and is designed to show and enable the progression of skills and knowledge from Early Years through to Year 6. This curriculum is delivered by a specialist Music teacher who has the experience, knowledge and ability to enable the children to make excellent progress in this highly-technical subject.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodiam Church of England Primary School - Computing
pageCache.text:
Computing
Intent
Our pupils will have a broad and deep understanding of how computing links to their own lives and experiences. They will develop analytical problem-solving skills and learn to evaluate and apply information technology. Underpinned by our whole-school commitment to helping our pupils to be equipped to become responsible members of a 21st Century society, our pupils will be empowered to be competent, confident and creative users of information technology. They will develop a love of the digital world and see its place in their future.
Good programmers know what to write. Great ones know what to rewrite and reuse.
Implementation
Our Computing curriculum encapsulates the National Curriculum and is designed to show and enable the progression of skills and knowledge from Early Years through to Year 6. We organise this teaching and learning across a two-year cycle to cater for our mixed-age classes.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodiam Church of England Primary School - English
pageCache.text:
English
Intent
Our pupils will develop a love of reading, writing and discussion and will be prepared for life as successful and socially responsible citizens. They will be inspired by a rich and varied literary heritage and will read widely and often. They will take pride in their writing and will write clearly, imaginatively and accurately, and adapt their language and style for a range of contexts. Our pupils will be confident in the art of speaking and listening and they will use discussion to communicate and further their learning in all areas of the wider curriculum.
Literacy is the bridge from misery to hope.
Implementation
At the Riverside Federation we provide an English curriculum that is ambitious and designed to help all learners to develop the skills and knowledge that they need to communicate effectively.
We are a ‘reading school' as we recognise that reading is a key life skill and a curriculum enabler. We focus on promoting a love of language and reading and ensuring that our children read as often and as widely as possible in order to improve their fluency and understanding.
Each class uses high quality, rich, class texts which are linked to their Learning Journey, to teach and inspire a range of reading and independent writing. Lesson sequences themselves build progressively towards an extended piece of writing.
We teach the National Curriculum and each year group bases its planning on a skills progression document which shows the clear progression of skills through each year group.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodiam Church of England Primary School - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
Intent
Children will have positive outdoor experiences in a natural setting. They will be resilient, confident and independent. They will be motivated, cooperative decision-makers with excellent social skills. They will have an understanding and empathy for the natural world.
Teaching children about the natural world should be treated as one of the most important events in their lives.
Implementation
We support the six principles of Forest School, which were agreed by the UK Forest School community in 2011 and we use these to underpin our planning and provision of Forest School at our School.

Geography
Intent
Our pupils will be able to reflect on their own values and beliefs, and those of others. They will know how to use atlases, maps and globes and have a good understanding of their locality and those further afield. They will be culturally aware and have an understanding of their responsibility to protect and preserve our planet.
Geography underpins a lifelong conversation about the earth as the home of humankind.
(Geography Association)

Our Geography curriculum encapsulates the National Curriculum and is designed to show and enable the progression of skills and knowledge from Early Years through to Year 6. We organise this teaching and learning across a two-year cycle to cater for our mixed-age classes.

History
Intent
Our pupils will think like historians. They will understand that history is a chronological narrative of real people in real places who lived in the past, and will recognise that they themselves are the people who will shape the future.
A people without knowledge of their past history, origin and culture is like a tree without roots.
Implementation

pageCache.pageTitle: Bodiam Church of England Primary School - Maths
pageCache.text:
Maths
Intent
Our pupils will have a deep, long-term and secure understanding of maths. They will be aspirational thinkers and resilient problem solvers. They will have an appreciation of the power of maths and its application to real-world scenarios. They will develop a 'maths is for everyone' mindset and be confident and competent mathematicians.
Mathematics is the most beautiful and most powerful creation of the human spirit.
Implementation
We follow the White Rose scheme for maths. Our Maths Mastery curriculum ensures that every child can achieve through practical, real-life, relevant experiences. A wide range of resources is used and pupils are taught to show their workings in concrete, pictorial and abstract forms. They are taught to explain their choice of methods and to develop mathematical reasoning skills. This mastery approach to maths allows children to make better sense of the world around them and gives them the ability to see patterns between mathematics and everyday life.

Reading and Phonics
Intent
Our pupils will develop a life-long love of reading and will be prepared for life as successful and socially responsible citizens. They will be inspired by a rich and varied literary heritage and will read widely and often. They will appreciate the work of different authors, poets and illustrators.
Show me a family of readers, and I will show you the people who move the world.
(Napoleon Bonaparte)
Implementation
We explicitly teach the core reading skills that children need (improving vocabulary, inferring, predicting, analysing, empathising explanation, retrieval, summarising) through whole class lessons. Explicitly teaching the key reading skills means that children have a good understanding of how writers make choices to have a specific effect on the reader, which in turn transfers into their writing. Each class reads a rich, class text which is linked to their Learning Journey.

Relationship, Sex and Health Education (RSHE)
Intent
Our pupils will form positive beliefs, values and attitudes. They will be prepared for the rich, diverse lives they will experience. They will be empowered and prepared to be excellent citizens in our 21st-century world as they will have the knowledge they need to be tolerant and respectful, and know how to seek appropriate support and safeguard themselves from any difficulties they may face.
The most important thing an institution does is not to prepare a student for a career, but for life as a citizen.
Implementation
We follow the Jigsaw scheme of work to deliver a robust RSHE curriculum. Through the use of Jigsaw, we deliver a whole-school approach to RSHE which includes mindfulness to allow children to advance their emotional awareness, concentration and focus. The programme is delivered in a spiral, progressive series of lessons which gives the children relevant learning experiences to help them navigate their world and develop positive relationships with themselves and others.

pageCache.text:
Religious Education
Intent
Our children will be prepared for life in a 21st century world. They will explore matters of religious and non-religious beliefs and find out what matters most to people in a wide range of traditions represented in our country and beyond. They will be discerning individuals who understand what is of value to themselves as they develop their own ideas and ways of living. They will be tolerant and understanding with the confidence to make their own informed decisions.
While the religious divisions in our world are self-evident, many people believe that religious conflict is always caused by a lack of education.
Implementation
We believe that Religious Education should be an exciting activity for all our children to share in, and regard it as a particular area of learning where Christian values and the school ethos can come alive in the classrooms. We employ a variety of teaching approaches to support the learning. We want to enable our children to think about themselves, their feelings, their relationships, and their uniqueness as human beings made in the image of God.
As a voluntary controlled Church of England School we follow the East Sussex Agreed Syllabus. We adopt an enquiry approach to teaching RE, covering Christianity, Hinduism, Islam and Judaism.
In accordance with our Religious Education policy and within the 1944 Education Act, parents may request that their child is withdrawn from all or part of Religious Education. Where parents wish to exercise this right, the Governing Body would first suggest that the parents meet with the Head of School or Executive Headteacher to discuss their concerns.

Science
Intent
Our pupils will think like scientists as they understand that Science changes our lives and is vital to the world's prosperity. They will recognise the power of rational explanation and develop a sense of excitement and curiosity about natural phenomena. They will understand the importance and relevance of Science to their lives now and in the future.
What is a scientist after all? It is a curious man looking through a keyhole, the keyhole of nature, trying to know what's going on.
(Jacques-Yves Cousteau)
Implementation
Our Science curriculum encapsulates the National Curriculum and is designed to show and enable the progression of skills and knowledge from Early Years through to Year 6. We organise this teaching and learning across a two-year cycle to cater for our mixed-age classes.

Wraparound Provision
Supporting busy families with quality care before & after school
Our wraparound provision runs Monday to Friday and offers families a safe, nurturing environment led by experienced staff, including fun activities and flexible booking options for busy schedules.
This is school-led convenient on-site care with affordable pricing, designed to support working parents.
Breakfast Club
Start the day right with a healthy breakfast at our breakfast club. This club runs from 8:00 am to 8:45 am. Children transfer directly to their classroom at the end of this session.
The cost of this session is £4.50 per pupil.
After School Club: Session 1
Session 1 runs from 3:15 pm to 4:15 pm and offers engaging, themed activities led by staff. These are pre-advertised to families on a termly basis and may include offers such as: cooking, art & craft, games etc.
The cost of this session is £4.50 per pupil.
After School Club: Session 2
Session 2 runs from 4:15 pm to 5:30 pm and is a relaxed environment with free play. Children are offered a healthy snack such as: bagel, crumpet, toast and spreads, with a drink.
The cost of this session is £4.50 per pupil.

The Riverside Federation
Bodiam C E School is federated with Etchingham C E School under the Riverside Federation. The schools share an Executive Headteacher and SENDCO and they are jointly governed by one Governing Board.
The rationale of the Federation is ‘better together.’ We believe that our partnership is a key driver in our pursuit of excellence so that we meet the needs and aspirations of all pupils as we work together within a culture of high expectation and continual improvement. Both schools in the Federation benefit through collaboration and sharing of best practice.
Benefits of our Federation include:
Pupil Events
Pupils come together and enjoy collaborating and co-operating together in learning opportunities which always have an element of peer challenge and stimulus. Most visits which enhance our exciting and relevant curriculum take place as joint ventures across peer classes / key stages.
Bodiam C E School visits Etchingham C E School every summer to perform their annual summer production.
Staff Collaboration and Professional Development
Staff across both schools share expertise and development opportunities. These include coaching, training and resources to support learning. Staff plan together with outcomes reflecting the individual classes for which they are responsible.
